prompt: Where does the lesson say a device's schema starts?

choices.text: From the tables the API returns, one per endpoint
choices.why: That is the usual first move, and the one the lesson argues against.

choices.text: From the server's database schema
choices.why: The server was designed for every client and every report.

choices.text: From the questions its screens ask
choices.why: Right. Each screen, its question, and how often.

choices.text: From the indexes SQLite suggests
choices.why: SQLite suggests none; the screens name them.

prompt: The server records which administrator last edited each course. Why does the planner's schema leave that column out?

choices.text: No screen reads it
choices.why: Right. It would be downloaded, stored, migrated and backed up for nothing, and it is somebody else's data.

choices.text: The server refuses to send it
choices.why: Nothing says it would refuse; the planner does not ask.

choices.text: SQLite cannot store names
choices.why: It stores text perfectly well.

choices.text: It would make the course list slower to sort
choices.why: Sorting does not read it; the cost is in keeping it at all.

prompt: Match each planner screen to what the lesson gives it.

pairs.right: counts stored on the course row
an id made on the device

right_distractors: a request to the server on every visit

prompt: In app mode, denorm.ts says Guitar has 2 sessions and 40 minutes after `s3` is removed. Why?

choices.text: The triggers ran as well as the app's code
choices.why: In app mode no triggers are created.

choices.text: The DELETE was refused by a foreign key
choices.why: The session was deleted; the check counted 1.

choices.text: resize() added the minutes twice
choices.why: resize touched Statistics, which is right at 95.

choices.text: remove() never touches the counts
choices.why: Right. Two of the three writes kept them; the third forgot.

prompt: A sync brings down a course row carrying the server's own session_count, and then its sessions, into a database with the lesson's triggers. What goes wrong if both are applied as they come?

choices.text: The triggers refuse a row written by the server
choices.why: Triggers do not know who wrote a row.

choices.text: The count is set, then raised again by every session's trigger
choices.why: Right. The totals are counted twice; only one of the two may be applied.

choices.text: The sessions arrive with no course and are dropped
choices.why: The course row came first.

choices.text: Nothing; the check corrects it at launch
choices.why: The check reports drift; it corrects nothing.

prompt: After `s5` is lengthened to 50 minutes, how many minutes does the course list show for Statistics?
Why does the week screen get an index rather than a stored total?

choices.text: Totals cannot be stored for dates
choices.why: They could; there would be one per possible week.

choices.text: Its answer depends on the week being looked at
choices.why: Right. There is no single number to keep.

choices.text: It is read rarely
choices.why: It is read on every launch.

choices.text: Triggers cannot run on the sessions table twice
choices.why: Several triggers already run there.

prompt: A phone and a tablet both last synced with six sessions. Offline, each adds one, with AUTOINCREMENT. What do they get?

choices.text: 7 and 8, because SQLite counts across devices
choices.why: Each database counts on its own.

choices.text: Two UUIDs
choices.why: That is the other run.

choices.text: An error, since the server has not answered
choices.why: AUTOINCREMENT needs no server.

choices.text: 7 and 7
choices.why: Right. A counter is unique on one database, and there are two.

prompt: Why does ids.ts print the length of each UUID rather than the UUID?

choices.text: The transcript has to repeat
choices.why: Right. randomUUID makes a new one every run; yours will be a different 36 characters.

choices.text: A UUID is a secret
choices.why: It is an identifier, not a secret.

choices.text: The terminal cannot show hexadecimal
choices.why: It shows it fine.

choices.text: The two would be equal and that would look wrong
choices.why: They differ; the program says so.

prompt: A UUID of version ___ puts a millisecond timestamp in its first 48 bits, so ids made one after another sort one after another.
An API insists on making ids itself. What does the lesson say the device keeps?

choices.text: Nothing until the server answers; the row waits unsaved
choices.why: Then nothing could be added offline.

choices.text: The server's id, guessed in advance as the next number
choices.why: A guess is the counter problem again, across every device.

choices.text: Two: its own, and the server's once it arrives
choices.why: Right. The local one is used for every local reference.

choices.text: A UUID, and the API is asked to accept it instead
choices.why: The API insists; the device cannot change that.

prompt: window.ts prunes everything older than 12 weeks that was sent. Why did `s17` survive?

choices.text: It was edited offline and never sent
choices.why: Right. On the device it is the only copy.

choices.text: VACUUM restored it
choices.why: VACUUM rewrites the file; it restores nothing.

choices.text: It belongs to a course
choices.why: Every session does.

choices.text: Its date is inside the window
choices.why: It is one of the old rows; the program counts it among them.

prompt: With a window of 12 weeks, how many sessions stayed on the phone in the lesson's run?
Which of these set the size of the window, according to the lesson? Choose all that apply.

choices.text: how far back the screens scroll
choices.why: A screen showing a year needs a year, or the network.

choices.text: what the server can send again
choices.why: Anything pruned must be fetchable again.

choices.text: how many unsent rows there are
choices.why: Unsent rows are never part of the arithmetic.

choices.text: the size of the server's database
choices.why: The server holds everyone; the device holds one person.

prompt: A planner keeps total minutes per course on the course row, updated by app code in add, edit and delete. A new feature moves a session to another course. What does the lesson's advice predict?

choices.text: Nothing changes, since the minutes are the same
choices.why: Two courses' totals change: one loses them, one gains them.

choices.text: SQLite moves the total with the row
choices.why: Nothing in the app-code version tells SQLite about the total.

choices.text: One more write path to keep in step
choices.why: Right. The lesson's trigger on UPDATE OF course handles it whatever code moved the row.

choices.text: The foreign key refuses the move
choices.why: Both courses exist.

prompt: Put in order what window.ts does.
items: work out the date the window starts
delete the old rows that were sent

prompt: Two devices create sessions offline with UUIDs, and later both rename the same course. Which problem from this lesson have UUIDs not solved?

choices.text: Two new sessions sharing an id
choices.why: That is exactly what UUIDs solve.

choices.text: None of this lesson's: two edits of one row is a conflict, lesson 13's subject
choices.why: Right. Unique ids keep new rows apart; they say nothing about two changes to one row.

choices.text: The window pruning the course
choices.why: Courses are kept whole; the window is for sessions.

choices.text: The stored count drifting
choices.why: A rename does not touch the counts.

prompt: Why must a row that has not reached the server never be pruned, however old?

choices.text: Old rows are needed by VACUUM
choices.why: VACUUM needs no particular rows.

choices.text: The server deletes it too when the phone does
choices.why: The server has never seen it.

choices.text: Its date is wrong
choices.why: Its date is fine; it is simply unsent.

choices.text: It is the only copy
choices.why: Right. Deleting it deletes what the person typed.
